outcome: perceived quality of midwifery and gynecological care
perceived willingness of healthcare providers to provide care
perceived adequacy of healthcare provider knowledge regarding specific perinatal care needs
cohort: The study included 22 women aged 29 to >35 years with total or partial visual impairment who gave birth after 2005.
finding: The primary finding was that 90.9% of visually impaired women perceived a lack of adequate knowledge among healthcare providers regarding their specific perinatal care needs.
followup_time: Up to the end of the puerperium period (typically 6 weeks postpartum)
